bubbles.label: Jealousy runs the night when the person you want leaves with someone else
bubbles.note: The stated subject: a man watching a woman he wants go home with another man.

bubbles.label: Repeating it was only a kiss keeps the loss small enough to hold
bubbles.note: The refrain shrinks the event every time it comes back, and never succeeds.

bubbles.label: The mind plays the scene in full detail and will not stop
bubbles.note: Cab, smoke, drag, chest, dress. Sleeplessness with a soundtrack.

bubbles.label: Announcing recovery at the exact moment the spiral restarts
bubbles.note: Coming out of my cage and I've been doing just fine, sung twice, identically, going nowhere.

bubbles.label: He names himself the optimist and keeps the name on
bubbles.note: Mr. Brightside is a title he awards himself mid-collapse. Eager eyes, open on purpose.

bubbles.label: Wanting everything gets called destiny rather than appetite
bubbles.note: Gotta be down because I want it all; destiny is calling me. Ambition language borrowed to dignify want.

bubbles.label: One kiss, and he has been grieving a relationship she never entered
bubbles.note: It started out with a kiss is the whole history. He is the only one who thought it started anything.

parent.label: Repeating it was only a kiss keeps the loss small enough to hold

bubbles.parentLinkRationale: Names what the minimising is protecting: not a broken relationship but a claim he never actually had.

bubbles.label: He supplies the cab, the smoke, the dress himself and calls it torture
bubbles.note: It's all in my head is an admission, not a defence. Nobody is showing him this. He keeps the projector running because stopping would mean she is simply gone.

parent.label: The mind plays the scene in full detail and will not stop

bubbles.parentLinkRationale: Turns the intrusive images into something he is doing, with a motive, rather than something happening to him.

bubbles.label: Losing her mostly means being the kind of man who loses her
bubbles.note: The rival gets described with more care than she does. What is unbearable is the ranking, not the absence.

parent.label: Jealousy runs the night when the person you want leaves with someone else

bubbles.parentLinkRationale: Moves the wound from LOVE to IDENTITY: the detail lavished on the other man shows this is about his own standing, not about missing her.

bubbles.label: I never asked her for anything, so betrayal is the flattering version
bubbles.note: The four unfinished I nevers are the only honest line in the song. Nothing was taken from me because I never put in a claim. If I say she wronged me, I was a man in a story; if I say I said nothing, I was a man in a room. I picked the story.

parent.label: One kiss, and he has been grieving a relationship she never entered

bubbles.parentLinkRationale: Deeper than mourning a relationship she never entered: he chose the mourning because the alternative admission is about him, not her — he never spoke, so this stops being a love story and becomes what he can stand to be

bubbles.label: I run the bedroom scene nightly because it is our only remaining contact
bubbles.note: The cab, the smoke, the dress — I direct all of it, in that order, every time. It's all in my head, and I keep the head running, because when the film stops she isn't thinking about me at all. Being sick to my stomach over her is the closest I get to being with her.

parent.label: One kiss, and he has been grieving a relationship she never entered

bubbles.parentLinkRationale: Stays in love, but implicates him: the grief isn't happening to him, he is manufacturing it frame by frame because the imagined betrayal is the only relationship still running

bubbles.label: I named myself Mr. Brightside so being passed over reads as personality
bubbles.note: Destiny is calling me, eager eyes, coming out of my cage doing just fine — I gave myself a brand name and a comeback arc for an evening that, from her side, contained one kiss and no sequel. The whole persona is scaffolding around a thing that was never big enough to need it.

parent.label: One kiss, and he has been grieving a relationship she never entered

bubbles.parentLinkRationale: The grieving needs a griever; he built a titled self out of one kiss, which moves the honest reading from what he lost to who he needs to be seen as

bubbles.label: I keep rewinding to the dress because part of me enjoys it
bubbles.note: The camera in my head does not linger on his face or their conversation. It goes to the drag of the cigarette, the hand on the chest, the dress coming off. I am directing this. I call it being sick to my stomach because the other word for what I feel watching her get undressed by someone else is unbearable to hold. I have imagined her more vividly since she left than I ever managed while she was in the room.

parent.label: He supplies the cab, the smoke, the dress himself and calls it torture

bubbles.parentLinkRationale: Moves from supplying the scene to wanting the scene. Naming which frames he chooses turns self-inflicted torture into appetite, and the category shifts to love because it is his own desire he is feeding, not his sanity he is losing.

bubbles.label: He simply did the thing I never got round to doing
bubbles.note: I never asked. I never said it. I never made the move that he made in one evening without apparently agonising about it. The film I run isn't really about her betraying me — it's a re-enactment of a man acting while I stood there being decent and patient and invisible. Every time I play it, I lose to him again, which is the only version of the story where I was ever in the running.

parent.label: He supplies the cab, the smoke, the dress himself and calls it torture

bubbles.parentLinkRationale: Says what the projector is actually screening. Not her leaving but another man's willingness beside his own. That is not a mental-capacity problem, it is a verdict on what kind of man he is, so it sits in identity.

bubbles.label: If it was only a kiss then I was never anything to her
bubbles.note: I keep repeating that it was only a kiss like it proves how small the crime was, but the size of the crime is the size of me. A betrayal means I had standing. A kiss she has already forgotten means I was a Tuesday. I would rather be the wronged man in a tragedy than the one she never really considered, so I keep the tragedy funded — the jealousy is the last evidence that we happened at all.

parent.label: He supplies the cab, the smoke, the dress himself and calls it torture

bubbles.parentLinkRationale: Keeping the projector running only makes sense if stopping costs him more than watching. What it would cost is his standing in the story, which is identity, not mind.

bubbles.label: It was only a kiss and I built a marriage on it
bubbles.note: He says it twice, like a lawyer weakening his own case. There was no us. He gave one night the weight of a claim so that this night could be a betrayal instead of what it is: someone he barely had going home with someone else. He is grieving a relationship he issued to himself.

parent.label: Losing her mostly means being the kind of man who loses her

bubbles.parentLinkRationale: The ranking only stings if he was ever in the running. Deeper than being the man who loses her is admitting he was never chosen at all — he manufactured the standing he is now defending. Sits in LOVE because the lie is about the relationship itself, not about his rank among men.

bubbles.label: I study him because I would rather be him than have her
bubbles.note: The smoke, the drag, the hand on the chest, the dress coming off — he has the man's whole evening blocked out shot by shot. She is barely in the frame as a person. What he is watching is a demonstration of how to be a man who gets taken home, and he is taking notes he will never use.

parent.label: Losing her mostly means being the kind of man who loses her

bubbles.parentLinkRationale: The focus notices he describes the rival more carefully than her; this names why. It is not comparison, it is wanting. He implicates himself by admitting the envy points at the man, which is why her absence never gets described at all.

bubbles.label: I replay it all night because nothing else makes me feel awake
bubbles.note: It's all in my head — he says it and keeps going anyway, adds detail, undresses her himself. Coming out of my cage, eager eyes: the sickness in his stomach is the strongest signal his body has produced in months. Being destroyed by this is more life than doing just fine ever was, so he keeps feeding it.

parent.label: Losing her mostly means being the kind of man who loses her

bubbles.parentLinkRationale: Being outranked would end when the night ends. He keeps the night running. Moves to FITNESS because the honest deeper reading is about his own appetite for the pain — a capacity problem, not a status one.

bubbles.label: The kiss registered on her side as the start of something
bubbles.note: Grief requires a thing that was jointly held. He is assuming she filed that night the way he did — as an opening rather than an evening. If she filed it as nothing, there is no ending to be confused by, only a man who kept a receipt.

parent.label: One kiss, and he has been grieving a relationship she never entered

bubbles.parentLinkRationale: You cannot grieve a relationship she never entered unless she at least noticed the door

bubbles.label: Tonight actually happened somewhere other than inside my head
bubbles.note: The cab, the smoke, the bedroom — I am not in that room and never was. For this to be grief there has to be an event. I have never checked whether there is a man at all, because checking could take the man away, and then I would have nothing to be destroyed by.

parent.label: One kiss, and he has been grieving a relationship she never entered

bubbles.parentLinkRationale: The grief needs an event tonight to be triggered by, not just a projector

bubbles.label: She would have said yes if I had ever actually asked
bubbles.note: The whole loss depends on her having been available to me and taken by someone quicker. If the honest answer was no, then nothing was taken — I was simply not the one, and the story collapses from tragedy into arithmetic.

parent.label: One kiss, and he has been grieving a relationship she never entered

bubbles.parentLinkRationale: Grieving what never started assumes it could have started and was intercepted

bubbles.label: One kiss is the largest thing that has happened to me
bubbles.note: For a single kiss to fund years of this, the rest of the ledger has to be empty. The size of my grief is a public statement about the size of my life.

parent.label: One kiss, and he has been grieving a relationship she never entered

bubbles.parentLinkRationale: The kiss can only carry this weight if nothing heavier ever arrived

bubbles.label: What I feel is grief and not an appetite I never fed
bubbles.note: Grief is respectable — it means I had her and lost her. Appetite means I wanted her and never said so, which is not a wound, it is a habit. I need the mourning frame because it makes the wanting retrospective and therefore blameless.

parent.label: One kiss, and he has been grieving a relationship she never entered

bubbles.parentLinkRationale: Calling it grief rather than unspoken want is what makes him the injured party

bubbles.label: It is her I want and not the position of being chosen
bubbles.note: I have never described her face. I have described a cab, a cigarette, a chest, a dress and a man. If what I lost was the slot rather than the person, then this was never a relationship she declined to enter — it was a vacancy I never applied for.

parent.label: One kiss, and he has been grieving a relationship she never entered

bubbles.parentLinkRationale: A relationship she never entered still assumes she is the thing he was after

bubbles.label: I could shut this off tonight and have decided not to
bubbles.note: Torture needs a torturer somewhere other than this bed. If the pictures arrive uninvited I am ill and blameless; if they arrive because I start them, then at 3am with the lights off I chose the cab, chose the smoke, chose the dress. I have never once tested which it is, because the test would take about four seconds and I would lose it.

parent.label: He supplies the cab, the smoke, the dress himself and calls it torture

bubbles.parentLinkRationale: He keeps the projector running only if it is his to stop. Otherwise he is a patient, not an author, and no self-implication survives.

bubbles.label: The film is the only thing scheduled for tonight
bubbles.note: For stopping to feel like erasure, the room has to be otherwise empty. If there were a job I cared about tomorrow, a friend expecting me, anything with a start time, the projector would be competing with something. It isn't. That is not her doing.

parent.label: He supplies the cab, the smoke, the dress himself and calls it torture

bubbles.parentLinkRationale: Stopping only equals losing her if there is nothing else in the night to move into.

bubbles.label: The only options are this film or never thinking of her again
bubbles.note: I have arranged the choice so that stopping means losing her completely. There is a third version where I sleep, and see her on Thursday, and say the sentence I have never said. I keep that one off the shelf because it requires me to speak while awake, in daylight, to her face, with the possibility of a no.

parent.label: He supplies the cab, the smoke, the dress himself and calls it torture

bubbles.parentLinkRationale: The film-or-nothing binary is what makes the torture look forced on him. It is his own arrangement, and it edits out the option that requires him to speak.

bubbles.label: The footage is accurate enough to count as news about her
bubbles.note: I admit I invented it and then I grieve it like a report. If I let myself notice that the drag of the cigarette and the hand on the chest are mine — my staging, my ordering, my choices — the sickness would have no source outside me and I would have to call it something other than what she did to me.

parent.label: He supplies the cab, the smoke, the dress himself and calls it torture

bubbles.parentLinkRationale: He can only call invented images torture if he still treats them as reportage about her rather than as his own staging.

bubbles.label: The but in it is all in my head reinstates the footage
bubbles.note: And it's all in my head, but she's touching his — chest now. The admission lasts half a line and the conjunction takes it back. He confesses to authorship and then keeps filming, in the same breath, without pausing for the contradiction.

parent.label: The footage is accurate enough to count as news about her

bubbles.parentLinkRationale: The line admits the head and then overrules it with but in the same breath — the exact mechanism of the assumption.

bubbles.label: Nobody in my life would ask me where these pictures come from
bubbles.note: The story holds because I am the only witness and the only source. One person close enough to say you weren't in that cab, were you, and the whole night collapses into a man alone with a habit. I have not built that person into my life. The solitude isn't a symptom of the heartbreak, it is the condition the heartbreak needs.

parent.label: He supplies the cab, the smoke, the dress himself and calls it torture

bubbles.parentLinkRationale: The framing survives unchallenged because there is no one in the room to ask where the footage came from — the isolation is load-bearing, not incidental.

bubbles.label: She is the reason for the film not tonight's casting
bubbles.note: If the same projector would run for the next woman who kissed me once — same cab, same smoke, same dress, different face — then this is not a loss I suffered, it is a facility I have, and it was running before she arrived and will run after.

parent.label: He supplies the cab, the smoke, the dress himself and calls it torture

bubbles.parentLinkRationale: If the projector would run for anyone, the torture is a standing capacity of his, not something she caused.

bubbles.label: The film gives me pain and nothing I go back for
bubbles.note: Torture is the word I have chosen. It only fits if there is nothing in me that returns to the bedroom scene for its own sake. If any part of me looks forward to the dress, then what I am doing at 3am is not being destroyed, it is visiting, and I have been calling it suffering to keep the visit clean.

parent.label: He supplies the cab, the smoke, the dress himself and calls it torture

bubbles.parentLinkRationale: The word torture requires that no part of him returns to the scene willingly.

bubbles.label: She compared the two of us and I placed second
bubbles.note: A ranking needs a contest. For me to have been outranked, she has to have held both of us in her head at the same moment and picked. I have never checked whether I was in the frame at all. Second place is a much better result than not being entered, so I have awarded myself second place and grieved it.

parent.label: Losing her mostly means being the kind of man who loses her

bubbles.parentLinkRationale: There is no second place unless a comparison was actually made by her.

bubbles.label: I have never once named the thing he has that I lack
bubbles.note: I know the cab, the smoke, the drag, the dress. I do not know what he has. I keep the deficit vague because a vague deficit is a condition and a specific one is a task. If I said out loud he stood up and spoke, then the difference between us is a sentence long and I could have said it by Thursday, and then tonight is not a verdict, it is a thing I skipped.

parent.label: Losing her mostly means being the kind of man who loses her

bubbles.parentLinkRationale: Being the kind of man who loses requires a difference in kind rather than a difference in what I did that night.

bubbles.label: Her choosing me was the rating I was waiting to be issued
bubbles.note: I have handed one woman on one night the authority to score me, and I accepted the score without appeal. That only makes sense if I had no other evidence of standing to weigh it against — nothing at work, nothing I am good at, no room where I am the one who gets picked. She did not rank me. I asked her to, silently, and then read the result.

parent.label: Losing her mostly means being the kind of man who loses her

bubbles.parentLinkRationale: Her verdict only ranks me if I have already accepted her as the judge; the ranking sits in EARNINGS because it is a standing I wanted certified, not a person I wanted.

bubbles.label: One Tuesday's outcome is a permanent statement about my type
bubbles.note: For this to be about the kind of man I am, tonight has to generalise. She went home with someone; that could be a mood, a week, a room, her business entirely. I have converted a single result into a category and moved into it. Being permanently the losing kind hurts more but explains everything, and I would rather have the explanation than the uncertainty.

parent.label: Losing her mostly means being the kind of man who loses her

bubbles.parentLinkRationale: One night only becomes an identity if it is treated as reporting on all nights.

bubbles.label: Someone other than me is keeping the score
bubbles.note: Humiliation needs a room. Being outranked only stings if the ranking is posted somewhere. Nobody watched this, nobody will mention it, no one is comparing us tomorrow. If I am the only person who knows there was a competition, then the ranking is not something done to me — it is a scoreboard I built, staffed and read aloud to myself in the dark.

parent.label: Losing her mostly means being the kind of man who loses her

bubbles.parentLinkRationale: Ranking is public by definition; if nobody else is counting, the humiliation is self-issued.

bubbles.label: If she had chosen me I would have stopped ranking myself
bubbles.note: The whole grievance assumes there is a top of this thing and that arriving there is restful. I have never tested it. If I had put her in the cab, I would have been in that bedroom counting the men before me, checking her phone in my head. The ranking is not something he won. It is the machine I run, and she was only tonight's occasion for it.

parent.label: Losing her mostly means being the kind of man who loses her

bubbles.parentLinkRationale: The ranking only hurts if winning it would have ended it.
